The Sun City Vendor Directory

The Vendor Directory is part of the SCHH Community Guide, a resident-built site for Sun City Hilton Head that also offers a community map, quick links to the services residents use most, weekly Deep Dives on topics that matter here, and an AI assistant that answers questions from Sun City's own publications, announcements, and meeting recordings.

Where the listings come from. We built the directory by researching about thirty categories of services residents need most — from electricians and HVAC to dentists and primary care — and listing the businesses that serve the Sun City area. Before a business is listed, we look it up online: is it real and currently operating, does it serve our area, and does it hold the state license its trade requires. The listing's Online verification line shows how much of that we could confirm — Extensive, Partial, or Limited. It's a note on our homework, not a grade for the business. Residents can also suggest a business that isn't listed yet.

What your neighbors say. If you've used a vendor, tell us with the I used this vendor button on their listing, add a comment about your experience if you like, and mark them as one you'd recommend. Each listing shows how many residents have reported using the business and how many recommend it. Where residents have left comments, the listing carries a short summary of what they said — not reviews to wade through, but a sense of how the work went, what people valued, and any cautions. Once residents report using a vendor, that count replaces the verification line; a neighbor's experience says more than our research does.

Research Briefs. For a bigger decision — a contractor for a major job, a new doctor or dentist — a Research Brief is a short, sourced report on one business. It checks the state license record directly, confirms who owns or runs the practice, lists each clinician's credentials and hospital affiliations for medical practices, separates what the business says about itself from what public records show, and ends with the questions worth asking before you hire. Where a brief already exists, it's on the listing for every verified resident to read. Where it doesn't, you can request one: the research takes considerable AI computing time, so a brief comes with a modest fee — and once written, it's shared with all residents, not just the person who asked. Briefs are prepared with AI-assisted research, checked against official records, and reviewed by a person before publication. A brief never ranks or endorses a business, and it never claims a "clean record" — public records can't prove the absence of problems. If we can't produce a useful brief, you aren't charged.

Who can read what. The directory and the verification line are open to everyone. Reporting use, recommending, and reading or requesting a Research Brief are for verified residents — sign in once with your email, and you're set.
